newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Los Pelambres sees partnership deal soon.
newsitem.headline: Chile Los Pelambres sees partnership deal soon.

text.p: The owners of Chile's Los Pelambres copper deposit expect to sign a final deal soon with a group of Japanese investors to carry out a $1.3 billion expansion at the pit, said a mining source.
"The company hopes to sign a partnership agreement within weeks. Everything is just down to very legalistic points," the source, who declined to be named, told Reuters.
Antofagasta Holdings plc signed a letter of intent in January to sell a 40 percent stake in the project to Nippon Mining and Metals Co and four other Japanese firms.
The London-quoted company is owned by Chile's Luksic group.
Finance for the mine should be finalized by the third quarter of the year, he said.
Banks and Japanese government institutions will fund 70 percent of the project, with the rest coming from the partners' own funds, he said.
Building work at the mine will start once the finance has been agreed and the project's recently completed environmental impact has been approved by local authorities.
Output at the pit will climb to 260,000 tonnes a year from 23,000 tonnes once the expansion is finished in 1999.
